verdict.rationale: Proa documents Suspense boundaries that stream ready chunks out of order so slow server data does not block the page, and it provides typed loader caching through WebContext, which covers the loading-UI side of the story. Nothing shows a resource primitive that turns server-loaded data into reactive state. Signals are mentioned only for client islands, not tied to loaded data. missing for 10: a documented resource/async-data primitive, reactive binding of server-loaded data to signals, fallback/loading-state API details for Suspense, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can treat server-loaded data as reactive state and build a responsive loading UI for it using resource and suspense primitives

citations.quote: let Suspense boundaries stream ready chunks out of order when slow data should not block the page
Every render has typed access to request-scoped data, response metadata, route state, and loader caching through the same WebContext
Add signals and event handlers, and Proa emits the server-rendered HTML plus the JavaScript required for that island
